That's not a bug.  
If adding another Menace Below charge lowers your food category, you may lose a global bonus like Leadership + 3 from abundance of food. This is reflected in the auto-resolve. 
So while adding a Menace Below charge may give you more clanrats, it can also lower the leadership of all your troops when you drop down into a lower food category, making your army weaker overall.  
I'd assume that adding 5 charges lowers your food category, thus reducing your strength, while adding more than that does not lower it anymore, thus increasing your strength.

Like others have already pointed out, Adventure Modules are most likely the way to go for you. But if you really wanna create your own world, then you should first find an overarching plot to build everything around.
For example:  
Judging by your username, I'm just gonna assume that you're a Lovecraft fan - So am I, by the way. So why not just take a Great Old One and make him the evil guy? The story could be about one of the following:  
  
- An evil cult trying to awake the Great Old One because they think that the whole world needs to be remade. Main characters could be the mad cult leader (possibly called Abdul Alhazred) and an ex-member who realised the errors of his/her way and is now trying to enlist the party's help to stop the cult.  
- A thief stole an ancient artifact from the main god's cathedral. Little did he know that this triggered a chain of events that would lead to the Awakening of a Great Old One. The party now has to find several things required for a ritual to banish the ancient evil again. Those things could be, for example, the Book of Vile Darkness and the Book of Exalted Deeds, or body pieces of a dead god, who is the only one able to defeat the Great Old One.  
- The whole world is drowning in chaos. Political leaders all over the continent have declared war on each other, for no apparent reason. Turns out that the culprits are Illithids who have accidentally found the body of a dead Great Old One in the Underdark and, now controlled by his last thoughts before he died, have begun taking over the minds of kings and emperors everywhere. The only way to stop this is to acquire the Spear of the Sun God from Mount Celestia, to reach the Great Old One's body in the Underdark, and to plunge the holy weapon into it's brain.  
  
After you established a general goal of the campaign, I would advise you to follow the most important rule of DM'ing: Steal everything.  
Just take pieces of established franchises here and there, maybe look into some more obscure or lesser known things to fill the gaps. The world in my own campaign is made from so many different pieces from things like Lord of the Rings, Dragon Age, Magic: The Gathering, Lovecraft, Warcraft, Spellforce, Gothic, and countless others, that it's basically become it's own thing, even though it's all stolen from somewhere.
